# config/splits.txt: which addresses of Crackdown 2 belong to which source file.
# Maintainer-owned ground truth. tools/check_integrity.py checks every claim in config/matched_functions.json
# against it. Contributors and agents never edit this file.
#
# <source file>
#   text <start> <end>   main-body range [start, end) in .text. Outside the order-list region the linker lays out each
#                        object's functions contiguously, so EVERY function in the range was emitted by this file's
#                        object, including inline/template functions from headers and surviving copies of folded code.
#   hot <addr>           a function of this file that the link order list moved into 0x821D0000-0x823D0000
#   init <addr>          the registrar's dynamic initializer
#   atexit <addr>        the registrar's at-exit destructor
#   folded <addr>        a function of this file that the linker folded (identical-code folding) into an identical
#                        copy owned by another file; the source still defines it, but it does not own the address
#
# Evidence for every entry below: the agents' recorded split decisions (tools/research/batch1, batch2, the pilots), the
# class's RetClassName/vtable/registrar, and the link-order check: the files' text ranges, initializers and at-exit
# destructors appear in the same order. Bootstrap script: tools/research/splits_bootstrap.py.
#
# Entries whose text comment starts with "auto:" were set up automatically from CD2's own structure (scripts and method:
# tools/research/scaffold/). Per registered class: its RetClassName (which returns the registrar's class-name string)
# identifies its primary vtable; its markers are RetClassName, MakeNew and the vtable functions no other registered
# class shares. The range runs from the first marker to the end of the last, so it never goes past the evidence:
# functions just before or after it stay unassigned until a maintainer extends it. Every auto entry passed these checks:
# no other class's marker and no function of another RuffKing object inside; no overlap; initializers in text order.
# Classes whose RetClassName comes from the same RuffKing object are one file.
